assertion_analysis.failure_condition: Returning an always-empty excerpt from should_trigger_fanout makes lines 95-97 and 105-107 red; the recorded negative control demonstrates exactly that (1 failed, 2 passed, EXIT=1).
Rendering an invented reason for a candidate with no failed checks, or dropping the (none) fallback from _build_proposer_user_prompt, reddens lines 118-122.
Letting a non-retrieval check contribute to the excerpt or to the trigger's maximum reddens lines 134-137; no production input is re-supplied on both sides of these assertions.

findings.text: non-blocking: check_results_from_failed_checks assigns failure_probability 1.0 to every persisted entry and never reads the veto flag, while imas_codex/standard_names/review/cascade.py:477 builds that list from the union of route.failed_checks and route.check_details. An answered-and-passing retrieval check therefore renders in the proposer prompt under 'Named checks this candidate failed', and because failed_check_reasons:121 falls back to the criterion when no reason is present, even a passed check with no judgment evidence is named. The over-firing of the trigger itself predates this change and lives in cascade.py, outside the node's write scope, but the new rendering is where the misstatement becomes visible to the proposer.

non-blocking: no test exercises the extraction cap _EXCERPT_MAX_CHECKS / _EXCERPT_MAX_CHARS (trigger.py:51-52), yet the evidence fragment states the cap as a delivered property; a regression that drops either bound passes the suite unchanged, so that claim rests on reading the code rather than on a guard.
